answer: I lock 42.7 POA on AT-11 for 55 minutes and plant four 1.6 m stakes along the north glacier tongue, each sighted from the 8.3 m tripod on knoll HN-2. Stakes ship only across the seasonal timber jetty at mile 2.1; a 12 mm numbered brass ferrule is crimped then sheared so it cannot be reused. Peers recompute spacing (18.4-19.0 m) and resection (0.00-0.06 m). A second AT-11 booking, or spacing within 0.08 m RMSE of another ticket, slashes 59 percent and retires AT-11. If cloud hides the tripod before stake 3, the remainder freezes 14 hours and a new transect is required, never the same ferrule.
